subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should Telegram first-run setup replace default pairing with token-verified owner allowlist capture, use a post-bootstrap owner-derived default flip, or preserve pairing as the default with stronger manual allowlist guidance?
rationale: The request changes who becomes authorized to command a Telegram bot during first-run setup and changes upgrade/default behavior for existing omitted dmPolicy configs, so automation cannot safely choose the trust model.

options.title: Token-Verified Owner Capture
options.body: Generate a short setup token, require the intended owner to send that token to the bot, then write dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom for that numeric Telegram ID while preserving explicit pairing configs.

options.title: Post-Bootstrap Default Flip
options.body: Keep first-run pairing unchanged and derive owner allowlist behavior from commands.ownerAllowFrom after the first approved owner, aligning this issue with the broader cross-channel default-flip design.

options.title: Keep Pairing Default
options.body: Leave runtime/setup defaults as pairing and improve warning, doctor, and docs guidance for users who want owner-only allowlist mode.

recommendation.title: Token-Verified Owner Capture
recommendation.body: Generate a short setup token, require the intended owner to send that token to the bot, then write dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom for that numeric Telegram ID while preserving explicit pairing configs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history signal across Telegram config defaults, runtime fallback, setup, docs, and prior review routing for this trust-boundary decision.
